text:
Predicates:
RankedHigh(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
Player(x) ::: x is a tennis player.
Female(x) ::: x is female.
Male(x) ::: x is male.
AtRolandGarros2022(x) ::: x participated in Roland Garros 2022.
QuestionedPlayer(x) ::: x is Coco Gauff.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHigh(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly, then they are one of the most active players.
∀x (LostTo(x, y) ∧ QuestionedPlayer(x) → RankedHigh(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 is ranked highly.
∀x (AtRolandGarros2022(x) ∧ Female(x) → LostTo(x, Iga Świątek)) ::: All female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (AtRolandGarros2022(x) ∧ Male(x) → LostTo(x, RafaelNadal)) ::: All male tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
∀x ((RankedHigh(x) ∨ LostTo(x, RafaelNadal)) ∧ QuestionedPlayer(CocoGauff) → ¬Male(CocoGauff)) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is not a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
AtRolandGarros2022(CocoGauff) ::: Coco Gauff is at Roland Garros 2022.

Conclusion:
¬(LostTo(CocoGauff, IgaŚwiątek) ∧ ActivePlayer(CocoGauff)) ::: Coco Gauff is not both a player who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 and one of the most active players in major tennis.
